title: Who will be the next Nebraska libero, Olivia Mauch or Laney Choboy?
text:
Two players. One jersey.
With the departure of (arguably) the greatest libero in NCAA Women’s Volleyball history Lexi Rodriguez from the Husker roster, the libero jersey is up for grabs. Rodriguez has made a huge impact on the Nebraska team and the sport of volleyball in general, so it’s no doubt that her shoes will be hard to fill. The Nebraska “littles” for the 2025 season consist of freshman Keri Leimbach, sophomore Olivia Mauch, junior Laney Choboy and senior Maisie Boesiger. While all amazing players, Mauch and Choboy are the two players in contention for the role of libero.
Mauch made her Husker debut last season competing as a true freshman, often being compared to Rodriguez due to her calm demeanor and excellent serve receive. Choboy on the other hand is entering her third season, known for her scrappiness and energy. There are so many aspects that Coach Dani Busboom Kelly will take into consideration when making the official decision, yet it’s certain that previous performance will be accounted for.
Of the two, which defensive specialist received more playing time in the 2024 season?


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggnewscale)
library(waffle)
library(gt)

vb <- read_csv("ncaa_womens_volleyball_players_2024.csv")

liv <- c("Sets" = 122, "Games Played"=36)
laney <- c("Sets" = 121, "Games Played"=36)

iron(
  waffle(
  liv,
  rows = 5,
  colors = c("red","black")
) +
   labs(
     x="Olivia Mauch",
     title="The battle of the littles", 
     subtitle="Which Husker DS had more playing time in 2024?") + 
   theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_blank()
  ),
waffle(
  laney,
  rows = 5,
  colors = c("red","black")
) +
  labs(
    x = "Laney Choboy",
    caption = "Source: NCAA | Graphic by Bailey O'Brien"
  )
)









One thing that’s for certain is that whoever earns the jersey will be sent behind the service line. In the 2024 season, Coach John Cook opted to not have Choboy serve and have her strictly in the back row, mainly covering the back right of the court. Mauch on the other hand was one of the most consistent Husker serves. Cook described her serve as “nasty,” and the numbers back that up as well. She made very few errors when serving as well.
Of the Huskers who served consistently, who’s service ace to error ratio was best?


Code
neblong <- vb |> 
  filter(team == "Nebraska") |> 
  filter(aces > 1) |> 
    select(name, s_err, aces) |> 
  mutate(sort = s_err + aces) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols=c(-name, -sort),
    names_to = "Stat",
    values_to = "Total"
  )

ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=neblong, aes(x=reorder(name, sort), weight=Total, fill=Stat)) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#d00000", "darkgrey"),
                    labels=c("Aces", "Service Errors")) +
  new_scale_fill() + 
  coord_flip()+
  labs(
    x="",
    y="Aces vs. Service Errors",
    title="Behind the service line",
    subtitle="Which Husker had the most aces and fewest errors?",
    caption="Source: NCAA | By: Bailey O'Brien"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
   theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )









Now what probably comes to mind first when thinking of the role of a libero, other than the fact that they wear a different jersey, is digs. This is the athlete expected to get every ball up and keep it from hitting the ground. The defensive specialists make a significant amount of digs as well.
The Big Ten is certainly the power conference of college volleyball. Of the top 15 libero/defensive specialists in the conference as a whole, where do the Nebraska players rank?


Code
b1g <- vb |> 
  filter(conference == "Big Ten") |> 
  filter(position == "L/DS")


b1g |> 
  select(name, team, digs, ret_att) |> 
  top_n(15) |> 
  arrange(desc(digs)) |> 
  gt() |> 
  cols_label(
    digs = "Digs",
    ret_att = "Serve Recieve",
    team = "Team",
    name = "Name" 
  ) |> 
   tab_header(
    title = "All over the court",
    subtitle = "Where do the Nebraska littles rank in digs in the Big Ten?"
   ) |> 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "black", weight = "bold", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("title")
  ) |> 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "black", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("subtitle")
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md("**By:** Bailey O'Brien  |  **Source:** NCAA")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = everything()),
    style = list(
      cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = px(3)),
      cell_text(weight = "bold", size=12)
    )
  ) |> 
  opt_row_striping() |> 
  opt_table_lines("none") |> 
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color= "#d00000"),
      cell_text(color = "white")
    ),
    locations = cells_body(
      rows = team == "Nebraska"))

The battle of the libero jersey is certainly going to be an intense one, as both Olivia Mauch and Laney Choboy have shown amazing capabilities and potential to fulfill this role. Statistically, Mauch slightly passes Choboy in nearly every category. However, being libero requires a lot more than what the stat sheet shows. It is a leadership position that can change the demeanor and direction of entire games. The longevity aspect is something to consider as well, as Mauch does have one more year of eligibility than Choboy.
At the end of the day, respecting Coach Dani Busboom Kelly’s decision is most important. These two are incredible athletes. Ultimately, the decision made is going to be what DBK believes will lead the Huskers to an extremely sought after national title, and no matter what both players are destined to make an impact on the team this season.

title: How will volleyball transfer Allie Sczech fit into Nebraska’s roster?
text:
Allie Sczech might just be exactly what the Huskers are looking for.
With the departure of five seniors and head coach John Cook, the Huskers have big shoes to fill in the 2025 season. The team has six incoming freshmen, along with redshirt freshman Skyler Pierce, who are eager to earn playing time this season. Another new player is Allie Sczech, an opposite hitter transferring in from Baylor. The incoming senior is a two-time All-Big 12 Second Team honoree looking to make an impact on the Nebraska roster.
Merritt Beason was the previous opposite hitter for the Huskers. She earned first team All-B1G honors during both of her years at Nebraska and was a key contributor for the team. Will Sczech be able to fill the shoes of Beason, or will another Husker fill the role instead?
How does Sczech’s hit percentage match up in the Big Ten, specifically with Nebraska’s attackers?


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggbump)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggnewscale)

vb <- read_csv("ncaa_womens_volleyball_players_2024.csv")

oppo <- vb |> 
  filter(conference == "Big Ten") |> 
  filter(
    position == "OPP" |
      position == "OH"
  ) |> 
  filter(s > 80) |> 
  top_n(30, wt=hit_pct) |> 
  mutate(PlayerTeam = paste0(name, ", ", team))

allie <- vb |> 
  filter(
    name == "Allie Sczech"
  ) |> 
  mutate(PlayerTeam = paste0(name, ", ", team))

opp_plus_allie <- bind_rows(oppo, allie)

neb <- oppo |> 
  filter(
    team == "Nebraska"
  )

ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=opp_plus_allie, aes(x=reorder(PlayerTeam, hit_pct), weight=hit_pct), fill = "lightgrey") +
  geom_bar(data=allie, aes(x=reorder(PlayerTeam, hit_pct), weight=hit_pct), fill = "#154734") +
  geom_bar(data=neb, aes(x=reorder(PlayerTeam, hit_pct), weight=hit_pct), fill = "#d00000") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
x = "", 
y = "Hit Percentage",
title="Sczech might just fit right in",
subtitle="Transfer Allie Sczech's 2024 hit percentage ranks her highly in the Big Ten and compared to Husker attackers.",
caption="Source: NCAA | By: Bailey O'Brien"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    ) 









Nebraska volleyball is known for having a very balanced offense, unlike other programs who constantly set their best attacker. During her time at Baylor, Sczech was a very efficient and reliable attacker. While the Big 12 and the Big Ten are different calibers of volleyball, Sczech’s numbers speak for themself and show her potential to dominate in a new conference.
Nebraska’s offense always gives its attackers plenty of opportunity, will Sczech be able to capitalize on this?


Code
attackers <- vb |> 
  filter(
    s > 80,
    total_attacks > 200
  )

neb <- attackers |> 
  filter(
    team == "Nebraska"
  )

allie <- attackers |> 
  filter(
    name == "Allie Sczech"
  )

neb_plus_allie <- bind_rows(neb, allie)

ggplot() + 
  geom_point(data=attackers, aes(x=total_attacks, y=kills), color="lightgrey") +
  geom_point(data=neb, aes(x=total_attacks, y=kills), color = "#d00000", size=2) +
  geom_point(data=allie, aes(x=total_attacks, y=kills), color = "#154734", size=2) +
  geom_text_repel(data=neb_plus_allie, aes(x=total_attacks, y=kills, label = name)) +
  labs(
    x="Attacks",
    y="Kills",
    title="Jumping on the opportunity",
    subtitle="Allie Sczech was a difference maker at Baylor. How does her number of kills compare to the rest of the NCAA?",
    caption="Source: NCAA | By: Bailey O'Brien"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
    theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    ) 









In the sport of volleyball, mistakes are inevitable. There will never be a libero that never lets a ball drop, a serving sub who is perfect every single serve, or an attacker who never makes an error. However, the goal is always to have as few mistakes as possible. Something good about measuring errors is that outside circumstances do not matter as much, and mistakes like these are generally on the attacker.
When comparing Sczech to last year’s Husker attackers, whose kill to error ratio is the smallest?


Code
vblong <- vb |> 
  select(team, name, position, errors, kills, total_attacks) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols=c(-team, -name, -position, -total_attacks), 
    names_to="Stat", 
    values_to="Total")

neblong <- vblong |> 
  filter(team == "Nebraska") |> 
  filter(position == "OH") |> 
  filter(name != "Skyler Pierce")


allielong <- vblong |> 
  filter(name == "Allie Sczech")


combinedlongvb <- bind_rows(neblong, allielong)


ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=combinedlongvb, aes(x=reorder(name, total_attacks), weight=Total, fill=Stat)) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("darkgrey", "#d00000")) +
  new_scale_fill() + 
  geom_bar(data=allielong, aes(x=name, weight=Total, fill=Stat)) +   
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("darkgrey", "#154734")) +
  coord_flip()+
  labs(
    x="",
    y="Kills vs. Errors",
    title="Striving for perfection",
    subtitle="Mistakes are bound to happen, which attacker has the fewest?",
    caption="Source: NCAA | By: Bailey O'Brien"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
   theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )









Sczech will make an immediate impact for the Huskers if she can beat out other players on the roster. She is at a slight disadvantage due to the fact that she is finishing her degree at Baylor, therefore is unable to participate in the beach and spring seasons.
Who will fill Merritt Beason’s role as opposite hitter for Nebraska? As of right now, signs point to Sczech.
